profile.campus: Salt Lake City metro, Utah (Flexential's Salt Lake City-market data centers, six named buildings across Salt Lake City, West Jordan, and Lindon)
profile.reading:
Flexential's own site publishes a facility page for this Lindon, Utah location at flexential.com/data-centers/ut/salt-lake-city/lindon-data-center, confirming it is part of Flexential's current Salt Lake City-market portfolio, but a direct fetch of that page returned a 403 error both in an earlier session and again when rechecked this session, most likely automated-access blocking rather than a missing or retired page. Three independent data center directories, Inflect, DataCenterHawk, and a Yelp business listing, agree on an address of 333 South 520 West, Suite 150, Lindon, Utah, and are treated here only as corroboration, not as a substitute for the operator's own page. No tier-1 or tier-2 source for this building's square footage or MW capacity was accessible this session, so those figures are not asserted; this is a deliberate, documented gap rather than a research shortfall. This building is one of six Flexential locations serving the Salt Lake City market, a secondary US data center hub built on some of the lowest electricity and natural gas rates in the nation (historically around 5 to 6 cents per kilowatt-hour), a cooling-efficient high-desert climate, and Utah's sales-and-use tax exemption for data center equipment purchases at facilities exceeding 150,000 square feet, retroactive to mid-2016. Other major operators active in the broader market include DataBank in Bluffdale, Aligned Data Centers in West Jordan, Novva Data Centers, QTS in Eagle Mountain, Meta, and Oracle. Seismic activity along the Wasatch Front is a real engineering consideration for the region's data centers, mitigated through structural design.

Flexential itself traces to the 1999 founding of ViaWest, which built out a Western US colocation footprint including Utah before merging with the Southeast-focused Peak 10 in 2017 and rebranding as Flexential in 2018; the company is now privately held with GI Partners as controlling sponsor. Utah's data center water use has drawn growing state scrutiny: a bill from Rep. Jill Koford, advanced unanimously by a legislative water panel in November 2025 for the 2026 session, would require data centers to report annual water consumption to the state under a $10,000-per-day fine for non-compliance, with individual figures kept anonymized publicly but available to state water officials. Reporting on the bill cited examples ranging from facilities using up to 5 million gallons a day, more than 12,000 times a typical household's usage, to the NSA's Bluffdale, Utah facility at about 23 million gallons annually, against low-water designs like Novva's reported 85,000 gallons; Koford said state water regulators had previously been left out of data-center water-use oversight, which had been handled mainly through city permitting.

reading.body:
Flexential Salt Lake City - Lindon is a confirmed facility in Lindon, Utah, operated by Flexential. The operator's own facility page exists but its published capacity specifications were not accessible this session, so no megawatt figure or rack count can be read from tier-1 sources. The address at 333 South 520 West, Suite 150 is corroborated across three independent directories.

Utah has 21 mapped data center facilities, of which 9 have published megawatt figures totaling 52.18 MW. This campus cannot be ranked within the state's published capacity since its own capacity is not published.

Without published specifications, this campus cannot be assessed for its relevance to AI scaling in the region based on power availability, cooling infrastructure, or compute density. Any reading of its role in the state's AI infrastructure requires the operator to publish its capacity.
